longForm.heroLead: Spin coating tells you a formulation works. It doesn't tell you whether that formulation will actually scale. FOM nanoRC closes that gap at the smallest possible footprint and cost. It's a benchtop slot-die coating machine that mimics the coating processes of large-scale roll-to-roll production, giving precise, reproducible, and scalable thin films from any solution or slurry precursor onto flexible substrates. A touch display controls drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, a built-in drying system handles the film after deposition, and the whole unit stays portable and light enough to move around a lab, with no scheduled maintenance required to keep it running.

body.text: The system deposits thin films from solution or slurry-based precursors onto flexible substrates, with a deposition length of 500 mm.
It's built to mimic the coating processes of large-scale roll-to-roll machines, giving a genuine miniaturized demonstration of industrial-scale slot-die coating rather than an approximation.

A touch display serves as the control panel, letting operators adjust drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself rather than a software-based one.
Key components include the touch display, a slot-die mounting gantry, adjustable feet, a removable drip tray, and a substrate support drum, with ventilation ducts and a power plug at the rear.
A drying system is built in, handling the deposited film as part of the coating process rather than requiring a separate step.
The machine doesn't come with an integrated syringe pump as standard, though FOM Technologies offers the option to combine the nanoRC with a compatible pump for precursor delivery.
Construction stays portable and compact, light enough to move around a lab, and the system is designed to run without scheduled maintenance or service.
It complies with the Machine Standards EN 60204-1 and ISO 13849-1 (CE), meeting the requirements of the 2006/42/EC Machinery Directive Annex II B.

paragraphs: Spin coating is fast and familiar, but it answers a narrower question than most research programs actually need answered.

Substrate size restraints, difficult batch processing, and a high percentage of material waste all limit how much a spin-coated result actually tells you about industrial viability. FOM nanoRC is built specifically to close that gap, replicating the coating process of large-scale roll-to-roll machines at laboratory scale, so results generated on the benchtop carry real, transferable relevance to pilot or production-scale coating lines. That makes it possible to develop or transfer thin-film knowledge directly into slot-die coating fabrication protocols, without the material consumption or hassle of a larger pilot line, while still supporting genuinely high-throughput experimental design.

body: How the touch display, gantry, and drying system work together on FOM nanoRC.
Every part of the coating process, from precursor delivery to the finished dried film, is handled through a small, purpose-built set of components.

The touch display sits at the center of daily operation, controlling drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself for turning the system on and off. The slot-die mounting gantry positions the coating head precisely over the substrate support drum, while a removable drip tray keeps runoff contained and cleanup simple between coating sessions. A built-in drying system processes the deposited film as part of the same workflow, and ventilation ducts at the rear manage airflow during operation. Because the system doesn't ship with an integrated syringe pump, FOM Technologies offers it as an optional combination, letting precursor delivery be matched to your specific formulation needs.

paragraphs: Film uniformity depends on more than just the coating head itself. How the substrate moves and how precisely that head is positioned both matter just as much.

Motorized height and tilt adjustment, accurate to +/- 1 µm, keeps the slot-die head positioned exactly where a formulation needs it, while an adjustable 0 to 90 degree coating angle gives control over deposition geometry beyond a single fixed setup. Bi-directional web handling with tension control manages how the substrate itself moves through the system, keeping tension consistent so the coated film doesn't distort or wrinkle during processing. Together, that combination is what delivers the uniform, reproducible dry film thickness the system is built around, from nanometers up through microns.

body: How FOM moduloR2R's automated logging and barcode sync keep large data volumes manageable.
Pilot-scale runs generate more data than manual documentation can realistically keep up with, and that's exactly the gap FOM moduloR2R's control software is built to close.

Complete coating conditions log automatically through the control software as a run proceeds, removing the need for manual record-keeping during production. Where physical traceability matters, that data can also print alongside the coated area itself using a synchronized barcode printer and reader, tying digital records directly to the physical film. Combined with process data export functions, that turns a pilot run into a genuinely analyzable dataset rather than a one-time production event.
